messages:
alex_support: Forwarding support ticket from customer (INC-12345): 'We noticed ~18 GPU-hours were billed to our Dedicated pool overnight but token burn stayed flat (~120 tokens). Dashboard shows no active requests. Invoice attached: https://invoices.redwood/example-INV-987. Can you triage?
priya_infra: On it — can you confirm pool id/name?
alex_support: Pool: redwood-prod-dedicated-42. Customer says they did not request burst. Invoice link above.
sam_sre: Quick thought: long-running pinned containers or stray jobs can count as uptime without token burn. Priya, can you run reserved_pool_uptime + worker heartbeat checks for that window?
priya_infra: Running quick query now:
```
SELECT sum(uptime_hours) AS hrs
FROM pool_usage
WHERE pool = 'redwood-prod-dedicated-42'
  AND ts >= '2026-12-10T00:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-12-11T00:00:00Z';
```
Result: 17.8 hours. Token burn (metering) for same window: 120 tokens.
priya_infra: curl to internal metering for raw events:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METERING_KEY}" "https://internal-metering/api/v1/pools/redwood-prod-dedicated-42/events?from=2026-12-10T00:00Z&to=2026-12-11T00:00Z"
```
metering-bot: ALERT: missing worker heartbeats detected for node gpu-74 between 02:30-03:00 UTC. Node recycled at 03:05 UTC.
sam_sre: If gpu-74 was recycled and there were processes pinned to it, the reserved hours would still be charged. Also check for any infra tasks accidentally scheduled on customer pools.
priya_infra: Pulled node logs from gpu-74 -> I see an infra smoke process 'jitter-checker' repeatedly initializing CUDA context every ~30s between 02:15-03:05. Service name: infra-monitor. The scheduler tagged it incorrectly and it landed in the customer pool.
alex_support: That would explain hours without token burn. Who owns infra-monitor tag config?
sam_sre: Paging @tomasz_billing for potential credit calc and billing impact.
tomasz_billing: Got it. From a billing POV we need: invoice id, exact hours, and a confirmation that the usage was non-customer-generated. Tentatively we can offer a credit for the 17.8h. Upstream fix: adjust allocation tags and re-run billing pipeline to produce corrected line items. Steps: 1) identify mis-tagged allocations, 2) patch allocation table, 3) re-run billing job for the invoice window, 4) issue credit if re-run is not feasible.
alex_support: Customer asked for timeline and remediation. I'll tell them we're investigating root cause and will propose a credit once confirmed.
priya_infra: Mitigation applied at 1934568150: removed infra-monitor from redwood-prod-dedicated-42 and added a guard in scheduler so only services with 'infra' tag can run in infra pools. Re-running allocation reassign job:
```
/bin/run_realloc --pool redwood-prod-dedicated-42 --window "2026-12-10T00:00Z/2026-12-11T00:00Z"
```
metering-bot: Billing reprocess queued: job_id=br-20261210-1934, status=queued.
tomasz_billing: Once the reprocess finishes we can either adjust the invoice or issue a credit. Estimated credit = 17.8h * rate_per_gpu_hour (will confirm exact dollar amount after pipeline gives final counts).
alex_support: :thumbsup: Updating ticket INC-12345 with timeline and planned credit. Will follow up when billing reprocess completes.
priya_infra: Follow-ups: add unit test for scheduler tagging, add alert for non-zero reserved uptime with token_burn < 100 tokens in the window, and add a nightly audit job that reports infra services scheduled into customer pools.
sam_sre: Thanks team — marking this as 'triage in progress'. Will close when billing-run completes and customer is updated.
